label: A fixed two-step XOR rule with four period-three suffixes
definition: TwoStepRule n f says that at every t at least n+1 the value f(t+2) is f(t) XOR f(t+1). parityTrace n a b keeps the observed all-true prefix and repeats a,b,a XOR b afterward. parityClass n admits exactly the four histories generated by the two Boolean seeds. constantClass n instead admits the two constant suffixes. The selector and cutoff are fixed within each comparison.
note: The recurrence is an equation on state values, not efficient causation or an existential supplier. Knowing the first two suffix values determines every admitted parity trace, while knowing only one bit at a later time does not determine its successor across the four traces. The construction is a positive mathematical control for retaining a higher-order constraint despite adjacent-pair richness; it does not prove any metaphysical view true or possible. The chosen selector depends on n, so it is not claimed rich after every longer observation of one fixed history class.
